problem: Deep-model object navigation agents trained end-to-end predict actions from visual observations and often fail in unseen environments when the target is not visible; prior knowledge about object/scene regularities is not used effectively for planning.
motivation: Humans navigate unseen environments using a cognitive map that stores past experience, anticipates what lies ahead, and is updated online. Giving an agent a similar structured prior that supports zone-level reasoning could improve navigation in unseen scenes.
key_idea: Build a hierarchical object-to-zone (HOZ++) graph over objects, zones and scenes that lets the agent identify current and target zones, plan an optimal zone path, and use the next zone as guidance, while updating the graph online from new observations.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract implies that zone-level, structured priors that are updated online serve as plug-in guidance for both end-to-end RL and modular methods.
method: HOZ++ graph: hierarchical graph encoding regularities among objects, zones and scenes.
Zone identification: determines the agent's current zone and the target's zone from observations.
Path planning: computes an optimal path between current and target zones and selects the next zone as guidance.
Online graph update: continuously updates the graph from real-time observations in new environments to adapt.
Versatile integration: plugs into end-to-end RL agents and modular navigation methods.

setting.backbone: not specified in abstract (end-to-end RL and modular methods augmented with HOZ++ graph)
setting.observation: visual observations (egocentric RGB likely; not specified)
